premises.statement: Account timezone values require no deterministic trimming or casing correction before applying the deletion rule.
premises.alternative: The general staging quality actions require automatically fixing "casing, whitespace trimming" and "standardize valid IANA timezones when pattern matches".
premises.reason: Correctable timezone values would otherwise cause entire account records to be discarded.

premises.statement: All non-null account timestamp and boolean values are directly castable to their declared output types.
premises.reason: An invalid value could prevent the staging SQL and pipeline from executing.

premises.statement: Twitter screen names containing harmful characters may be retained if removing those characters produces a nonempty name.
premises.alternative: The description says "rows with NULL/blank or harmful characters are removed", which could require testing harmful characters in the original value.
premises.reason: The interpretation determines whether potentially unsafe source records survive staging.

premises.statement: A Twitter URL with a valid-looking prefix remains acceptable even when the rest of the value is not a valid URL.
premises.alternative: The staging quality documentation describes nullifying an "optional URL fails regex", which may mean validating the whole field rather than a prefix.
premises.reason: The unanchored ending can retain malformed optional URL values.

premises.statement: All non-null Twitter profile timestamp and boolean fields used in direct casts are castable to the declared types.
premises.reason: Malformed source values would make execution fail rather than produce cleaned profiles.

premises.statement: Organic report account_id identifies the Twitter user whose profile should enrich the tweet.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: left join users u on u.id = o.account_id and u.row_num = 1
premises.alternative: The material index also exposes raw.tweet.user_id and raw.tweet.account_id; tweet.user_id could be the required profile join key.
premises.reason: Using an account identifier as a user identifier can leave most profiles missing or attach the wrong users.

premises.statement: raw.tweet.full_test contains the tweet text referred to as full_text in the contract.
premises.alternative: The contract explicitly says "Tweet text joined from raw.tweet.full_text", while the material index lists only full_test.
premises.reason: The implementation resolves a schema discrepancy without establishing the substitute field's meaning.

premises.statement: Each tweet identifier has at most one matching row in raw.tweet after conversion to BIGINT.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: left join tweets t on try_cast(o.organic_tweet_id as bigint) = t.tweet_id
premises.reason: Duplicate matches would multiply report rows and their downstream metrics.

premises.statement: The most recently synced Twitter profile is the intended profile for every report date, and no conflicting profiles tie at that sync time.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
premises.alternative: The source is named twitter_user_history and reports contain date; the contract says only that user attributes are "joined from raw.twitter_user_history" without defining latest versus historical selection.
premises.reason: Profile attribution can change across historical reports or become nondeterministic on ties.

premises.statement: The organic tweet output should strip disallowed characters from raw user screen names rather than preserve the joined source value.
premises.alternative: This model's screen_name description says "From raw.twitter_user_history.screen_name"; the explicit screen-name cleaning rules are specified separately for stg_social_media__twitter_user_history.
premises.reason: This changes the reported identity text and can create empty names without the profile model's row filtering.

premises.statement: Facebook staging impressions should use the maximum lifetime metric rather than the specified staging default of zero.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: max(post_impressions) as impressions ... coalesce(pm.impressions, 0)::bigint as impressions
premises.alternative: The contract defines impressions as "Default 0 in staging" and lists only post history and page data as this model's source tables.
premises.reason: This introduces an additional source and changes a core performance metric for matched posts.

premises.statement: Every qualifying Facebook post has at most one row in raw.facebook_pages_post_history.
premises.alternative: The source includes updated_time and is named post_history, so multiple versions may require selecting a version.
premises.reason: Repeated versions would produce duplicate posts and potentially retain outdated visibility states.

premises.statement: The latest synced Facebook page record is the intended page metadata for all posts, regardless of deletion status.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last ... pg.row_num = 1
premises.alternative: raw.facebook_pages_page_data includes _fivetran_deleted, which is not consulted when selecting page metadata.
premises.reason: Deleted or historically inappropriate page versions could supply names and follower counts.

premises.statement: A Facebook post with a null is_hidden value should count as visible.
premises.alternative: The contract describes the model as "Published, visible Facebook posts" but does not define whether unknown visibility qualifies.
premises.reason: This determines whether posts with unknown visibility enter reporting.

premises.statement: Facebook post created_time and the numeric and boolean fields directly cast by this query contain only compatible values.
premises.reason: An incompatible source value could abort the model rather than be corrected or nullified.

premises.statement: Instagram metrics should select the first non-null media-specific field in a fixed priority order independent of the post's media_type.
premises.alternative: The contract refers to normalized "mi.impressions" and other normalized metrics without defining this priority; the inspected rows contain simultaneous non-null carousel, story, photo/video, and reel metrics.
premises.reason: The chosen priority can select the wrong metric family for most non-carousel posts.

premises.statement: Each media identifier has at most one matching Instagram insights row across all source_relation values.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: left join insights i on m.id = i.id
premises.alternative: The insights table exposes both source_relation and _fivetran_id, but neither participates in the join or deduplication.
premises.reason: Multiple matches would multiply posts and metrics.

premises.statement: Each qualifying Instagram media identifier occurs only once in media history.
premises.alternative: The history source includes _fivetran_id and _fivetran_synced, but no media-version selection is performed.
premises.reason: Multiple historical versions would create duplicate post outputs.

premises.statement: The latest synced Instagram user record supplies the intended account metadata for every historical media post.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
premises.alternative: The contract requests account details "from user history" but does not specify latest rather than post-time values.
premises.reason: Account names, follower counts, and media counts can differ materially across versions.

premises.statement: Instagram media user_id and user-history id identify accounts in the same identifier namespace.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: left join users u on m.user_id = u.id
premises.alternative: The material index exposes both id and ig_id in Instagram user history, and their relationship to media user_id has not been checked.
premises.reason: A namespace mismatch would remove account enrichment from otherwise valid posts.

premises.statement: LinkedIn post_message should prefer article_title, then media_title, and use commentary only as a fallback.
premises.alternative: The contract lists post_message without defining this priority; the available history source contains commentary, which could instead be the post message.
premises.reason: The priority can replace the actual post commentary with a content title.

premises.statement: Each LinkedIn post has at most one matching post-content row.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: left join raw.linkedin_pages_post_content pc on pc.post_id = regexp_replace(o.ugc_post_id, '^urn:li:share:', 'urn:li:share:')
premises.alternative: The content source includes media_id and _fivetran_id, which could distinguish multiple content items for one post.
premises.reason: A post with multiple content items would be emitted multiple times.

premises.statement: Each LinkedIn post has at most one matching UGC history row.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: left join raw.linkedin_pages_ugc_post_history h on h.id = o.ugc_post_id
premises.alternative: The source is a history table with last_modified_time and _fivetran_synced, but the query selects no single version.
premises.reason: Multiple versions would duplicate posts and produce conflicting messages or timestamps.

premises.statement: LinkedIn organization-post identifiers can be matched literally to history and content identifiers without reconciling share and ugcPost URNs.
premises.alternative: The samples show organization-post IDs beginning "urn:li:share:" and history IDs beginning "urn:li:ugcPost:"; the implemented replacement leaves the identifier unchanged.
premises.reason: Unreconciled identifier forms could leave messages and creation timestamps missing across many posts.

premises.statement: LinkedIn organization-post records with null organization identifiers should be deleted from staging.
premises.alternative: The contract declares organization_id as VARCHAR without a not_null constraint or delete_row rule.
premises.reason: This adds an undocumented row-exclusion rule.

premises.statement: The maximum channel_subscribers across all YouTube channel-basic records is the intended subscriber count for every video on that channel.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: select channel_id, max(channel_subscribers) as channel_subscribers ... group by channel_id
premises.alternative: The channel-basic source includes date, while the contract specifies only "COALESCE(channel_info.channel_subscribers, 0)" and does not define maximum-over-time selection.
premises.reason: A historical maximum can systematically overstate subscriber counts.

premises.statement: Each qualifying YouTube video identifier occurs only once in raw.youtube_video.
premises.reason: Duplicate source identifiers would produce duplicate videos and metrics.

premises.statement: All YouTube publication timestamps and numeric metric values used by the query are compatible with its casts and arithmetic.
premises.reason: Malformed values could prevent pipeline execution.

premises.statement: A missing YouTube channel title should produce the literal page_name 'Unknown Channel'.
premises.alternative: The contract declares page_name as VARCHAR but provides no default or correction rule for it.
premises.reason: This changes only the labeling of records with missing titles.

fewer.reason: The remaining projections, identifier filtering, and timezone regex directly implement explicit contract requirements; no further material unsupported premises were identified.
The other field mappings and conversions follow explicit contract definitions, and the model performs no joins or history selection requiring additional key assumptions.
The remaining time-window, view-data filter, URL construction, metric defaults, and rate formulas are explicitly specified.
